newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM says euro should be strong vs dlr, yen.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM says euro should be strong vs dlr, yen.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Friday that Europe's future euro currency should be strong and stable, and that Europe did not want a weak euro to keep the continent's exports competitive.

"There is no desire in Europe for a weak euro vis-a-vis the dollar and the yen to make our exports more competitive," Lipponen said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery on his visit to Japan.
On the contrary, "there is widespread understanding that a relatively strong euro would be beneficial", he said, noting that exchange rate stability would benefit all.
A copy of the speech was distributed to Finnish media.
The future euro currency would become "one of the three main currencies in the global economy", together with the U.S. dollar and the yen, Lipponen said.
"It seems likely that the euro will float against the dollar and the yen," he added.
In Europe, internal stability was a primary aim amid efforts to solve structural problems, he said.
"A strong and stable euro will contribute to this and toward stability in the major currencies as well and benefit the global economy in general," Lipponen said.

"The achievement of EMU will eradicate the obstacles to growth stemming from intra-EU currency turbulence," he said. Progress already made towards implementing EMU had already had a positive effect on exchange rate stability, he added.
Commitment by EU countries to budget consolidation and reduced deficits had helped long- and short-term interest rates converge at lower levels, Lipponen said.
"In this way we are crerating the right conditions for sustained growth and job creation," he said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
